clue.text: Bloody paperwork, huge amount where trials are conducted

parts.note: B is the printed euphemism for the swear word bloody, as in b----y
admin is office paperwork
a ton is colloquially a huge amount

explanation.surface: Someone cursing an enormous pile of office forms at a courthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trials' suggests a court, but Badminton in Gloucestershire hosts famous equestrian horse trials.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton House in England stages the annual Badminton Horse Trials, an eventing competition.

clue.text: Flipping layabout drinking whiskey in basins

indicators.note: drinking means the reversed layabout takes the next letter inside it
flipping turns the word for the layabout over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a slob is a lazy layabout
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An exasperated complaint about a idle loafer knocking back spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowls are round deep dishes, the same vessels as basins.

clue.text: Conscientious lord holding Athletic and United up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the whole construction is read from the bottom
holding means the word for lord contains the next pieces

parts.note: lud is the form of lord used to address a judge, as in m'lud
athletic means fit
U is the abbreviation for United in football club names

explanation.surface: A diligent peer supporting two football clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Athletic and United' look like team names but give FIT and U; LUD holding FITU, then read upwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dutiful person is one who carefully does what duty requires, which is being conscientious.

clue.text: Implant — it's left in accidentally

indicators.note: accidentally signals that the letters fall into a new, unplanned order

explanation.surface: Someone explaining that an object got left inside by mistake, perhaps after surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil an idea is to implant it gradually in someone's mind.

clue.text: Fruit with a sharper taste, one left for later and nine cored

indicators.note: left for later means the letter for one is moved further along in the word

parts.note: tangier means having a sharper taste
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: cored means the middle letters of the number are taken out

explanation.surface: A recipe note about a tangy fruit, setting one aside and coring nine others.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the I of TANGIER later gives TANGERI; NINE without its core IN gives NE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small citrus fruit like a mandarin orange.

clue.text: Norse jug? Or more recent?

parts.note: N is an abbreviation for Norse
a ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: Asking whether an old Scandinavian pitcher is in fact a later piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Newer is the comparative of new, meaning of more recent origin.

clue.text: Violin returns for fast movements

indicators.note: returns means the word for the violin comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin

explanation.surface: A violinist coming back in for the quick sections of a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movements' suggests music, but the answer means quick dashes.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to move suddenly and swiftly, so darts are quick dashes.

clue.text: Doses of medicine from medic, anything at all with sulphur

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic
aught is an old word meaning anything at all
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A doctor prescribing any old remedy as long as it contains sulphur.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is a single dose of liquid medicine, swallowed in one go.

clue.text: From what we gather family is in tatters

indicators.note: is in means the word for family sits inside the word for tatters

parts.note: rags are tatters, torn clothes
kin means family

explanation.surface: Hearsay that a family has fallen on hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From what we gather' reads as 'apparently', but the definition is literal: what a rake gathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rakings are the leaves and debris collected with a rake, so literally what is gathered.

clue.text: Clock adjusted? Quite a long time to hang around

parts.note: set means adjusted, as a dial is set

indicators.note: to hang around means the long time is draped about the word for quite

parts.note: an eon is a vast period of time
Quite! is an exclamation of agreement, like yes

explanation.surface: Having reset the clock, someone faces a long wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clock' looks like a timepiece but is the slang verb for noticing.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang to clock someone is to notice or look at them, the same as to catch sight of.

clue.text: Power units seeing delays after I left for short time

indicators.note: left for means the letter I departs and something else takes its place

parts.note: waits are delays
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An electricity reading affected by queues once someone briefly steps out.
explanation.definitionFit: The watt is the SI unit of power, so watts are units measuring it.

clue.text: Unfolding sales opportunity for a racecourse

parts.note: something unfolding is just emerging, so new
a market is an opportunity to sell

explanation.surface: A business pitch about a developing commercial opening for a horse-racing venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket in Suffolk is a famous English horse-racing course and training centre.

clue.text: Over half in area around 10 reserve for do

indicators.note: over half keeps more than half the county name, its first four of seven letters

parts.note: Suffolk is the English county around the racecourse at 10 across
ice is a cool reserve of manner

explanation.surface: A cryptic instruction about stockpiling in the region near the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: SUFFOLK is the eastern English county containing 10 across; four of its seven letters are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: To do in the sense of 'that will do' means to be enough, which is to be sufficient.

clue.text: Georgian post-Reformation clergymen left mass out

indicators.note: post-Reformation read as after re-forming, so the remaining letters are rearranged
out means the letters for left and mass are taken from the clergymen

parts.note: M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Church history: Protestant clergy of the Georgian age who dropped the Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: CLERGYMEN without L and M leaves CERGYEN, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Regency was the late part of the Georgian period in Britain, so Regency style is Georgian.

clue.text: Very depressed hearing such a piece?

indicators.note: hearing means the phrase is to be taken as spoken

parts.note: very depressed is so low

explanation.surface: Someone feeling miserable while listening to a mournful piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo is a musical piece performed by one player alone.

clue.text: Do the vocals when full of scotch and jamming

indicators.note: full of means the singing word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: doing the vocals is to sing
to scotch a rumour is to quash it

explanation.surface: A singer at a jam session after a few whiskies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' suggests whisky but is the verb meaning to suppress.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamming things together is cramming or squashing them into a tight space.

clue.text: Spurs mess up tie with rioting

indicators.note: rioting suggests wild disorder, so the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Tottenham Hotspur fans causing trouble at a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spurs' looks like the football club but is the plural noun for stimuli.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurs as in incentives are impetuses, forces that drive action forward.

clue.text: These changes in the country of France, they show what's due to the workers

definitions.text: they show what's due to the workers

parts.note: pays is the French word for country

indicators.note: changes means the letters of that word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark about shifting labour relations in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Paysheets are records listing the wages owed to each employee.

clue.text: Coppers catching group in piratical centre in G&S opera

indicators.note: catching means the coins enclose the next piece

parts.note: coppers are copper coins, pence

indicators.note: group in, with centre, takes a group of letters from the middle of piratical
centre, with group in, says the letters come from the middle of the word

explanation.surface: Police arresting a gang in the middle of a Pirates of Penzance production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piratical' nods to Gilbert and Sullivan's Pirates of Penzance; its middle three letters give ATI.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is a comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, satirising aesthetes.

clue.text: Utterly heartless he plans to break inside — this is not pretty

indicators.note: inside means the rearranged letters go within the outer letters
heartless removes everything but the first and last letters
to break means those letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A burglar plotting a break-in, with a moral comment that it is ugly behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unshapely lacks a pleasing form, so it is not pretty to look at.

clue.text: Average as well as, at heart, a vaguely unpleasant person

indicators.note: at heart means the conjunction sits in the middle of the word for average

parts.note: so-so means average, middling
and means as well as

explanation.surface: A mild verdict on someone who is mediocre and rather disagreeable at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A so-and-so is a euphemism for an annoying or disliked person.

clue.text: Where water flows in the open ocean

definitions.meaning: a water pipe under the street carries the supply
the high seas, as in the Spanish ...

explanation.definitionFit: A water main is a principal supply pipe, and the main is a poetic term for the open sea.

clue.text: Being a professor attached to the Authorised Version I can be seen in flowing gown

parts.note: AV is the abbreviation for the Authorised Version of the Bible

indicators.note: flowing means the gown's letters, with the I, move freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A cleric in academic dress, steeped in the King James Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Professor' is not an academic but one who professes; 'can be seen in' just places I with GOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to declare openly, so avowing is professing, the act of a professor in that sense.

clue.text: Last 60% of official announcement is unparalleled

indicators.note: last 60% of keeps the final six of the ten letters, dropping the start

parts.note: a communiqué is an official announcement

explanation.surface: A press release judged to be unmatched, at least in its closing portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unique has no equal, so it is unparalleled.

clue.text: Oil platform put back in position surrounded by the briny

indicators.note: in means the reversed platform goes inside the word for position

parts.note: a seat is a position, as a seat in parliament

indicators.note: put back means the platform word is turned around

parts.note: a rig is an oil platform

explanation.surface: An offshore rig being towed back to its station at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea-girt is a poetic adjective for land encircled by the sea, the briny being slang for the sea.

clue.text: Idiot, just the ultimate duff president

indicators.note: just the ultimate keeps only the final letter of that word

parts.note: duff is slang for the backside, the rump

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a hopeless head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump served as President of the United States.

clue.text: Where to find eggs when heading off to a supermarket

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of that word

parts.note: the Co-op is a British supermarket chain

explanation.surface: Telling someone where eggs are while they set off shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: The Co-op is a cooperative chain of British food shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen coop is the enclosure where hens are kept and lay.

clue.text: Hot rod's parking fine about to be overturned

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
OK means fine

indicators.note: to be overturned means the two letters are turned upside down in this down entry

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A souped-up car's parking ticket about to be quashed on appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot rod' looks like a car but is a fire iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker is a metal rod for stirring a fire, so it gets hot.

clue.text: Legal document needed for one new false tooth?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a denture is an artificial tooth or set of them

explanation.surface: A dentist drawing up a contract before fitting a replacement tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: An indenture is a formal contract, historically binding an apprentice.

clue.text: Sharp-witted bogus doctor after one-to-one heart transplant

indicators.note: heart transplant means the middle letter of the doctor word is replaced

parts.note: a quack is a fake doctor
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sham surgeon performing a heart operation after a private consultation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-to-one' says the heart letter A is swapped one for one with I.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick in the sense of quick-witted means mentally sharp and alert.

clue.text: Bird moves tail around to protect egg

indicators.note: to protect means the moving word encloses the egg letter
tail around means the final letter of that word is moved back around its neighbour

parts.note: goes means moves
O looks like an egg

explanation.surface: A bird shifting its tail feathers to shelter its egg.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the tail letter S of GOES back one place gives GOSE, which then holds O.
explanation.definitionFit: A goose is a large waterbird related to ducks and swans.

clue.text: He's driven to overtake green convertible

parts.note: to pass a vehicle is to overtake it

indicators.note: convertible means the letters can be converted into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A driver going past a green open-top car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convertible' looks like a car but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger is someone carried in a vehicle that another person drives.
